citation: Mohr AE, Minicucci O, Long D et al. (2021). Resistant Starch Combined with Whey Protein Increases Postprandial Metabolism and Lowers Glucose and Insulin Responses in Healthy Adult Men. Foods 10(3):537.
protocol: Four pancake breakfasts, crossover: waxy maize starch (WMS; 73 g carbohydrate, 5 g fat, 15 g protein, 0 g fibre listed), WMS + 20.5 g whey, RS4 resistant starch (hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate) at the same 73/5/15 g, RS + whey. Venous blood at 0, 60, 120, 180 min (no blood for WMS + whey).
population: n=8 men, generally healthy, non-smokers; age and BMI in Table 2 (mean ± SD).

reports.where: Table 5: estimated marginal means (95% CI) at 0, 60, 120, 180 min per meal

note: Paired-meal contrast, fibre: waxy maize starch pancake vs resistant starch (RS4) pancake at matched grams of carbohydrate, fat and protein (whey arms are a protein-amount add-on, not a source contrast). Clean starch-for-resistant-starch swap at identical macronutrients. Watch: insulin row is labelled only "(units)" (looks like µIU/mL), values are model-estimated marginal means with 95% CI, Table 1 lists fibre as 0 g for the RS meal (RS4 counted in carbohydrate), n=8.
